abel-beth-maacah.title: Abel-beth-maacah
abel-beth-maacah.note: Named once, in 2 Samuel, and nowhere else.

abel-beth-maachah.title: Abel-beth-maachah
abel-beth-maachah.note: A fortified city in the far north near Dan. Its own people called it a mother in Israel, which is how you said a town led the region. Joab besieged it to get at the rebel Sheba, and it was taken later by Ben-hadad when Asa paid him to attack, then by Tiglath-pileser.

abiathar.title: Abiathar
abiathar.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
abiathar.note: He was the only priest to get out of Nob alive when Saul had the place killed, and he went straight to David and stayed his priest through the running years and the reign. At the end he backed Adonijah instead of Solomon, and Solomon sent him away from the priesthood rather than kill him.

abigal-2.title: Abigal
abigal-2.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
abigal-2.note: A different woman of the same name from the same years, named only in genealogical lists.

abimelech.title: Abimelech
abimelech.note: Gideon's son by a concubine. He killed almost all seventy of his brothers to clear his own way, which is most of what Judges has to say about him.

abishai.title: Abishai
abishai.about: David's warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
abishai.note: David's nephew, and the most willing man he had. He is credited with three hundred killed on his own. Twice he offered to finish one of David's enemies on the spot, Saul asleep in the camp and Shimei cursing on the road, and both times David told him no.

abishalom.title: Abishalom
abishalom.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
abishalom.note: This is Absalom, David's third son. He killed his half-brother Amnon for raping their sister Tamar, and when David punished neither of them he spent years quietly building support before taking the throne by force. The revolt ended with his famous hair caught in an oak while he was still riding.

adoram.title: Adoram
adoram.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
adoram.note: The same man as Adoniram, over the forced labour for David and Solomon. Years later Rehoboam sent him to collect tribute from the northern tribes in the crisis that split the kingdom.

ahilud.title: Ahilud
ahilud.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ahilud.note: Two of his sons served kings: Jehoshaphat was David's royal recorder, and Baana governed one of Solomon's twelve districts.

ahimaaz.title: Ahimaaz
ahimaaz.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
ahimaaz.note: Zadok's son, who carried intelligence to David during Absalom's rebellion. After the battle he raced another messenger to be first with the news.

ahithophel.title: Ahithophel
ahithophel.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
ahithophel.note: David's most trusted counsellor, whose advice was treated as if it came from God. He went over to Absalom. When Absalom turned down his plan for a rival counsellor's, Ahithophel saw the rebellion was finished, went home, put his affairs in order and hanged himself.

amasa.title: Amasa
amasa.about: Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy
amasa.note: David's nephew. He led Absalom's rebel army, and afterwards David offered him command of the whole royal army to win back Absalom's supporters. Joab, jealous, stabbed him while pretending to greet him with a kiss.

ammiel.title: Ammiel
ammiel.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ammiel.note: 1 Chronicles 3:5 makes an Ammiel the father of Bathsheba, called Bath-shua there. The name also turns up in 2 Samuel 9 and 17, given only as a father's name.

ammihud-3.title: Ammihud
ammihud-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ammihud-3.note: A man from the united kingdom, and 2 Samuel is the only book that names him.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amnon.title: Amnon
amnon.about: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
amnon.note: David's firstborn. He raped his half-sister Tamar, with a cousin's scheme to help him, and David did not punish him. Two years later her full brother Absalom had Amnon murdered, and that was the start of the road to Absalom's revolt.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

archi.title: Archi
archi.note: Hushai's clan. He was the loyal friend of David who worked against Ahithophel's advice during Absalom's rebellion.

baal-hazor.title: Baal-hazor
baal-hazor.note: Absalom held a sheep-shearing feast there, on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin, and used it to have his men kill Amnon. It was revenge for what Amnon had done to their sister Tamar.

bahurim.title: Bahurim
bahurim.note: A village east of Jerusalem, on the road down to the Jordan Valley. Shimei the Benjamite lived there. When David fled during Absalom's revolt, Shimei came out to curse him and throw stones.

barzillai.title: Barzillai
barzillai.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
barzillai.note: When David fled from Absalom, this old and wealthy Gileadite fed him and his men. David later offered him a place at court. Barzillai turned it down.

bath-sheba.title: Bath-sheba
bath-sheba.about: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
bath-sheba.note: She was Uriah the Hittite's wife. David saw her bathing, sent for her, and got her pregnant while Uriah was away fighting in David's own army. The cover-up ended with Uriah's death in battle, arranged by David.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

benaiah.title: Benaiah
benaiah.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
benaiah.note: He commanded David's bodyguard, and before that he was known for killing a lion in a pit on a snowy day. He also beat an Egyptian giant by wrestling the giant's own spear off him and killing him with it.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

berites.title: Berites
berites.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
berites.note: The Berites turn up once, among the groups Joab passed through while chasing the rebel Sheba son of Bichri to Abel of Beth-maachah. Nobody is sure who they were. Some read the name as a slip for Bichrites.

beth-maachah.title: Beth-maachah
beth-maachah.note: The northern city Sheba fled to when his revolt collapsed. The people inside threw his head over the wall to end the siege.

bichri.title: Bichri
bichri.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
bichri.note: Sheba's father, and Sheba was the Benjamite who led a short rebellion against David not long after Absalom's revolt was crushed.

cherethims.title: Cherethims
cherethims.about: A military group in the Old Testament
cherethims.note: David's bodyguard, with the Pelethites, under Benaiah's command. They were tied closely to the Philistines and likely came from Crete.

chimham.title: Chimham
chimham.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
chimham.note: The son of Barzillai, the old Gileadite who stood by David in Absalom's rebellion. David took Chimham back to Jerusalem as the reward. Property near Bethlehem seems to have carried his name for generations.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling the largest territory Israel ever held, which Solomon then inherited. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

eliam.title: Eliam
eliam.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
eliam.note: Bathsheba's father, called Ammiel in Chronicles. A son of Ahithophel with the same name was one of David's thirty. If they are one man, Bathsheba was Ahithophel's granddaughter, and some see that behind his betrayal of David in Absalom's revolt.

en-rogel.title: En-rogel
en-rogel.note: A spring just south of Jerusalem where the Kidron and Hinnom valleys meet. Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited there to carry news to David in Absalom's revolt, and Adonijah held his feast there to make himself king. Many put it at Bir Ayyub, Job's Well.

ephraim-2.title: Ephraim
ephraim-2.note: Named twice, in 2 Samuel and John, and nowhere else.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gera.title: Gera
gera.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
gera.note: He is only ever named as Shimei's father, and Shimei is the Benjamite who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion.

geshur.title: Geshur
geshur.note: It was a small Aramean kingdom northeast of Galilee, and Absalom ran there after murdering his brother Amnon and stayed three years under his grandfather the king.

gibeon.title: Gibeon
gibeon.note: They tricked Joshua into a treaty by dressing as travellers from far away, the Hivites of this city northwest of Jerusalem, and so they lived but served at Israel's sanctuary. The tabernacle stood at Gibeon for years, and Solomon had his dream there. At el-Jib dozens of jar handles stamped with the name have settled where it was.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gileadite.title: Gileadite
gileadite.note: Someone from Gilead, east of the Jordan, or of the clan named after Machir's son. Jephthah is the best known, the judge who beat the Ammonites and made the rash vow about his daughter.

giloh.title: Giloh
giloh.note: Ahithophel came from Giloh, in Judah's hill country southwest of Hebron. When Absalom took Hushai's advice over his, he went home to Giloh and hanged himself.

gilonite.title: Gilonite
gilonite.note: It is what Ahithophel is called, since he came from Giloh. He was David's trusted counsellor, then Absalom's, and he hanged himself when his advice was turned down.

gittite.title: Gittite
gittite.note: A man from Gath. Obed-edom the Gittite kept the ark in his house before David brought it up to Jerusalem, and Ittai the Gittite brought his foreign troops to David's side when Absalom rebelled.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hushai.title: Hushai
hushai.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
hushai.note: David's friend, who stayed behind when Absalom rebelled so he could work from inside Absalom's court. Ahithophel gave Absalom sound advice, Hushai talked him into a worse plan, and the time it bought saved David.

ira-3.title: Ira
ira-3.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
ira-3.note: One of 3 men called Ira. This one is a man from the united kingdom, named once in 2 Samuel.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

ithai.title: Ithai
ithai.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
ithai.note: Ittai, a Philistine commander from Gath, who would not leave David when Absalom rebelled, though David offered to release him. David gave him a third of the army.

ithra.title: Ithra
ithra.about: Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy
ithra.note: Amasa's father, and Amasa led Absalom's army against David. Ithra married Abigail, David's sister, so Amasa was David's nephew. Samuel calls him an Israelite; Chronicles calls him Jether the Ishmaelite.

jairite.title: Jairite
jairite.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jairite.note: Ira, who served David as a priest or chief officer, carries this label, which ties him to Jair. He closes the list of David's court officials, after Joab, Benaiah and Jehoshaphat the recorder.

jedidiah.title: Jedidiah
jedidiah.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
jedidiah.note: "Beloved of the LORD." Nathan gave the baby Solomon this name at God's direction, right after the story of David and Bathsheba and the death of their first child, but Solomon is the name that stuck.

jehoiada-2.title: Jehoiada
jehoiada-2.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoiada-2.note: Known through his son, the commander of David's bodyguard who carried out the killings after David's death, in Samuel and Kings.

jehonadab-2.title: Jehonadab
jehonadab-2.about: David's nephew living at the time of United Monarchy
jehonadab-2.note: 2 Samuel names him once, and he is a man from the united kingdom.

jehoshaphat-2.title: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat-2.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
jehoshaphat-2.note: David's recorder, the official who kept the court's records, and he still held the post in the next reign.

jerubbesheth.title: Jerubbesheth
jerubbesheth.note: Gideon again, under a name used only in 2 Samuel 11:21. The scribe swapped the -baal ending of Jerubbaal for -besheth, "shame", rather than write Baal's name. Ishbaal became Ishbosheth and Meribbaal became Mephibosheth the same way.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

joab.title: Joab
joab.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
joab.note: David's nephew, and the commander of his army for most of the reign. He was loyal to what David needed rather than what David said: he arranged Uriah's death when asked, killed Absalom when told not to, and murdered Abner and Amasa under cover of friendship. David never forgave him. On David's word Solomon had Joab killed, even holding on to the altar.

jonadab-2.title: Jonadab
jonadab-2.about: David's nephew living at the time of United Monarchy
jonadab-2.note: David's nephew, clever and crooked, who gave Amnon the scheme that got his half-sister Tamar alone, and the rape and the killing that followed started there.

jonathan-2.title: Jonathan
jonathan-2.about: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
jonathan-2.note: A priest's son who ran messages to David from inside the city during his son's revolt, and once had to hide in a well to do it. He also brought word that a new king had been crowned.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kidron.title: Kidron
kidron.note: The valley along Jerusalem's east side, between the city and the Mount of Olives. Reforming kings dumped smashed idols and temple rubbish into it, and Jesus crossed it with his disciples on the way to Gethsemane the night he was arrested.

lo-debar.title: Lo-debar
lo-debar.note: A town where, in 2 Samuel 9, a lame son of the old royal house is found living in another man's home. Amos plays on its name, which sounds like "nothing."

machir-2.title: Machir
machir-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
machir-2.note: Not Manasseh's son. This Machir kept a lame son of the old royal house in his home, and later brought supplies to a king running from his own son's revolt.

mahanaim.title: Mahanaim
mahanaim.note: "Two camps." Jacob met the angels of God here near the Jabbok River on his way home, and split his household in two before facing Esau. After Saul died, Ishbosheth ruled the northern tribes from Mahanaim while David held Hebron, and years later David fled there himself from Absalom and heard there that his son was dead.

mephibosheth.title: Mephibosheth
mephibosheth.about: Jonathan's son living at the time of United Monarchy
mephibosheth.note: Jonathan's son, lame in both feet since his nurse dropped him running from the news that Saul and Jonathan were dead. Years later David found him, gave him back Saul's land and a seat at the king's table for Jonathan's sake. During Absalom's rebellion a servant accused him of disloyalty, and his grief and unkempt state when David came home suggest the charge was false.

nahash-4.title: Nahash
nahash-4.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
nahash-4.note: A king from the united kingdom, and 2 Samuel is the only book that names him.

nahash-3.title: Nahash
nahash-3.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
nahash-3.note: Named once, at 2 Samuel 17:25, as the parent of Abigail and so of Amasa. Whether Nahash there is a man or a woman is an old question: the verse calls Abigail 'daughter of Nahash' while 1 Chronicles 2:16 makes her Jesse's daughter, and readers have squared that either by taking Nahash as another name for Jesse or as the name of Jesse's wife.

nathan.title: Nathan
nathan.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
nathan.note: The prophet who told David the story of the rich man who took a poor man's only lamb, let David condemn the man, and then turned it on him over Bathsheba and Uriah. Earlier he had brought God's promise that David's house would last forever. When David was dying, Nathan helped put Solomon on the throne ahead of a rival half-brother.

pelethites.title: Pelethites
pelethites.note: They always come paired with the Cherethites, as David's personal guard under Benaiah. The names sound foreign, and they were probably hired soldiers of Philistine or Aegean background.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

rabbah.title: Rabbah
rabbah.note: Capital of Ammon. David's army besieged it, and Uriah died in that siege, put where the fighting was worst on David's orders.

rogelim.title: Rogelim
rogelim.note: Barzillai's town in Gilead. He was the old, wealthy man who fed David's camp during Absalom's revolt, and afterward he turned down the king's offer of a place in Jerusalem and sent Chimham instead.

saul.title: Saul
saul.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
saul.note: Israel's first king, found while he was out looking for his father's lost donkeys and anointed by Samuel in private before the tribes confirmed him.

sheba-2.title: Sheba
sheba-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
sheba-2.note: He raised a revolt against David in 2 Samuel 20 and called the northern tribes away from him. It ended at a walled town, with his head thrown over the wall to the men outside.

sheva.title: Sheva
sheva.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sheva.note: There are two. One is a son of Caleb in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2:49), and the other is one of David's scribes, likely the same official called Seraiah elsewhere.

shimeah.title: Shimeah
shimeah.about: David's adversary living at the time of United Monarchy
shimeah.note: The man who came out cursing David as he fled Jerusalem, throwing stones and calling him a man of blood. He is from Saul's house, which is the point of it.

shimeah-3.title: Shimeah
shimeah-3.about: David's brother living at the time of United Monarchy
shimeah-3.note: David's brother, a son of Jesse. His son Jonadab was the shrewd nephew who helped Amnon get Tamar alone.

shobi.title: Shobi
shobi.about: Ammonite living at the time of United Monarchy
shobi.note: Son of Nahash, the Ammonite king. When David ran from Jerusalem in Absalom's rebellion, Shobi brought food and bedding for him and his men.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

talmai.title: Talmai
talmai.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
talmai.note: A king of Geshur, whose daughter Maacah married David and bore Absalom.

tamar-4.title: Tamar
tamar-4.about: Absalom's daughter living at the time of United Monarchy
tamar-4.note: A man from the united kingdom, and 2 Samuel is the only book that names him.

tamar.title: Tamar
tamar.about: David's daughter living at the time of United Monarchy
tamar.note: David's daughter, raped by her half-brother Amnon. David did nothing, and her full brother Absalom had Amnon murdered for it.

tekoite.title: Tekoite
tekoite.note: Someone from Tekoa, the hometown of Amos. The wise woman Joab sent to David about Absalom was a Tekoite, and so were at least two of David's mighty men.

thebez.title: Thebez
thebez.note: Abimelech, Gideon's son who made himself king, was besieging the tower at Thebez when a woman dropped a millstone on his head. He told his armor-bearer to kill him so nobody could say a woman did it. Joab still remembered it years later.

uriah.title: Uriah
uriah.about: Bathsheba's husband living at the time of United Monarchy
uriah.note: Uriah the Hittite, one of David's best soldiers and Bathsheba's husband. David got her pregnant while he was at war and tried to get him to go home to her, and Uriah would not while his comrades were still in the field. So David had him put where the fighting was worst and left there to die.

zadok.title: Zadok
zadok.about: High Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
zadok.note: The priest who stayed with David through Absalom's rebellion. He would have carried the ark out with the king, and David sent it back. Zadok anointed Solomon, and when Abiathar backed Adonijah and was sent away, Zadok was left as the only high priest.

zeruiah.title: Zeruiah
zeruiah.about: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
zeruiah.note: David's sister, the mother of Joab, Abishai and Asahel. David said the sons of Zeruiah were too much for him.

ziba.title: Ziba
ziba.about: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
ziba.note: A servant of Saul's house. David put him in charge of Mephibosheth's land, and during Absalom's rebellion Ziba told David that Mephibosheth had turned against him. It was a lie, and it cost Mephibosheth half his property.
